summary: Electron runbook launcher fails to authenticate: SSO authn_hint mismatch for embedded webview sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Users report that the internal Runbook Launcher (Electron desktop app) intermittently fails to complete SSO sign-in when the flow uses the embedded webview. The error presented is a generic 'Unable to authenticate' dialog and the app logs show an Okta SAML/OIDC response being rejected due to an authn_hint mismatch.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers on call cannot launch runbooks that require elevated access during their shift (affects PagerDuty on-call rotation).
- Blocks emergency runbook execution and increases Mean Time to Resolution for operational incidents.

Observed behavior:
- Webview navigates to Okta, user authenticates successfully, but on redirect back to the app the identity-proxy rejects the assertion with: 'authn_hint mismatch: expected electron_app, got electron-webview'.
- Affected sessions show a short-lived cookie created by a legacy proxy path (/auth/electron) while current proxy expects /auth/desktop.

Expected behavior:
- Electron app webview completes SSO and grants a session token consistent with other clients (browser, CLI).

Initial logs/snippets:
- identity-proxy: "WARN auth: assertion rejected - authn_hint mismatch (expected=desktop, received=webview) tx=0x9c71"
- electron app: "INFO sso: received redirect URI with state=..., code=...; token-exchange failed: 403"
- Okta debug logs (partial): "Redirect URI matched, but relayState contained legacy client_id 'runbook-launcher-legacy'"

Workaround so far:
- Short-term: instruct affected users to use the web console (browser) instead of the Electron app to run critical runbooks.
- Support has temporarily allowed a permissive mapping in the identity-proxy config for 24 hours for 'runbook-launcher-legacy' clients in us-east-1 while we investigate.
steps_to_reproduce: Install the internal Runbook Launcher Electron app (v2.4.1) on macOS or Linux.
Launch the app and click 'Sign in with SSO'.
Complete the Okta sign-in in the embedded webview.
Observe the webview redirect back to the app and note the error dialog 'Unable to authenticate'.
Check identity-proxy logs for authn_hint mismatch for that transaction ID.
logs: [identity-proxy] 2026-03-10T15:22:04Z WARN auth: assertion rejected - authn_hint mismatch (expected=desktop, received=webview) tx=0x9c71
[electron-runbook] 2026-03-10T15:22:05Z ERROR sso: token-exchange failed status=403 body="Forbidden"
comments: Support (Aisha): Captured initial user reports from #support. Reproduced with macOS 13.4 and Electron v21. Reproduced reliably when webview uses the legacy client_id.
Oncall (Miguel): Scoped the issue to identity-proxy authn_hint validation. Temporarily allowed legacy client_id in identity-proxy mappings for us-east-1 to unblock users (24h).

SRE (Priya Kaur): Adding identity-proxy diagnostics to trace authn_hint and relayState. Suggest validating Electron upgrade path; previous desktop packaging moved from client_id 'runbook-launcher-legacy' to 'runbook-launcher-desktop' causing mismatch.

Dev (Connor Lee): Proposed fix to accept legacy relayState when combined with new client_id and to add a migration shim in the Electron app to update stored client_id on first run. Preparing PR for identity-proxy change.
Support (Aisha): Communicated browser workaround to affected on-call engineers and logged names for targeted follow-up.
investigation_notes: Reproduction confirmed on macOS and Ubuntu when app config still references legacy client ID in embedded webview header.

Okta confirms the assertion contains a relayState parameter that the proxy expects to match a current client mapping. If it doesn't match, the proxy treats the assertion as potentially replayed or from a deprecated client and rejects it.
Telemetry shows ~0.4% of active desktop users still have the legacy client_id in their persisted app config (likely from v2.2.x).
Identity-proxy mapping implementation performs strict equality on authn_hint; suggests relaxing matching logic to accept known legacy aliases for a migration window.

Risk assessment: relaxing matching introduces minor spoofing risk if combined with open redirecters; mitigation is to restrict relaxation to signed client metadata and region-specific mapping (us-east-1 only initially).
resolution: Short-term mitigation: identity-proxy mapping relaxed for 'runbook-launcher-legacy' in us-east-1 for 24h to unblock oncall. Medium-term fix: PR #1824 updates identity-proxy to accept configured legacy aliases for a 30-day migration window and adds audit logging. Desktop app PR #341 will migrate stored client_id on first launch to canonical 'runbook-launcher-desktop'. Next steps: complete PR review, deploy identity-proxy change to staging, run focused e2e with instrumented logs, then promote to prod. Follow-up: email campaign targeted at 0.4% of users with legacy installs and add upgrade enforcement in v2.5.0.
next_steps: Complete code review and merge PRs (#1824, #341).
Deploy identity-proxy change to staging and run regression test suite focused on SSO flows.
Monitor auth rejection rate in us-east-1 for 72 hours post-deploy; rollback plan ready if error rate increases >2x baseline.
Notify support and oncall channels once migration shim is live and schedule a follow-up to mark the issue Resolved.
